claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 6 years old.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards his care - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, and I'm not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand this situation a bit more:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and how long has it been since he stopped living with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex's mum claiming Child Benefit for him, or do you know if anyone else is claiming it for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if she's claiming it or not. I don't know if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough to assess your situation.

Based on what you've told me, let me explain the eligibility for Child Benefit in your circumstances:

To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to be responsible for a child. You're usually considered responsible if either:
- You live with the child, OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep, you would not meet the responsibility criteria for claiming Child Benefit for him.

Additionally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If Alex's mum is claiming it (which is likely since he lives with her), then you would not be able to claim it anyway.

Let me record my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. 

However, if your situation changes in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you start making regular financial contributions towards his upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit amount - you may become eligible to claim. In that case, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office, as only one person can claim for each child at a time.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
